msrv.policy: CI and package updates keep the workspace buildable on the declared MSRV; the current floor follows DataFusion 55.1.0, kube 4.2.0, and the internal materialized view runtime.

package_reviews.subject: datafusion
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use DataFusion for ad hoc SQL and Parquet scans through Velorix query policy gates; do not make it durable authority.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Upgrade through the DataFusion release train and keep DataFusion-version-specific policy evidence explicit.

package_reviews.subject: object_store
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use object_store for authoritative create/read/list/range behavior through Velorix capability probes; keep authority and DataFusion scan client boundaries explicit.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Unify duplicate object_store versions when DataFusion and authority-path dependencies converge without weakening create-only semantics.

package_reviews.subject: kube
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use kube for Kubernetes coordination, CRDs, watch, and Lease APIs only; object storage remains database authority.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Upgrade with the kube release train and keep generated CRD/Lease evidence current.

package_reviews.subject: k8s-openapi
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use the Kubernetes API version set selected by kube and CI; avoid hand-written Kubernetes wire types.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Advance with kube compatibility requirements and regenerate CRD evidence when supported cluster APIs change.

package_reviews.subject: slatedb
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use exact crates.io SlateDB 0.16.0 with default-features=false, default GC, and durable commit acknowledgments. The user accepts the measured upstream storage-cost increase over the former fork. See docs/development/slatedb-upstream-comparison-2026-09-27.md for the original failed gate, scoped baseline recalibration, durability and bidirectional compatibility evidence. This is not an external audit. Do not duplicate SlateDB storage internals in Velorix.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Review future official releases against durability, persisted-state compatibility, default-config cost gates and dependency checks. Preserve the 25% gate budget and require documented measured evidence for baseline changes.

package_reviews.subject: foyer
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use Foyer only as a non-authoritative cache; never use it as durable database state.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Replace or disable Foyer if cache behavior conflicts with authority-path object storage or SlateDB ownership.

package_reviews.subject: rhizadb
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use exact crates.io rhizadb 0.19.0 for the metadata service. Local tests cover authenticated peer identities, WAL continuity, and operator-managed generation recovery without PVCs. Backend-authoritative bounded time and production multi-writer safety remain unproven; preserve fail-closed admission. This is not an external audit.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Review published SDK upgrades against metadata conformance, peer authentication, and generation-recovery tests before changing the pin.

package_reviews.subject: materialized_view_runtime
package_reviews.feature_policy: Use the internal jarless materialized view runtime for admitted views; do not add external compiler, package-loading, or image-managed execution paths.
package_reviews.replacement_plan: Grow supported SQL families inside the internal runtime with admission tests and fail closed for unsupported shapes.

exceptions.reason: Two lines coexist in the all-features graph: foldhash 0.1.5 for hashbrown 0.15.5 (petgraph 0.8.3, tokio-util 0.7.19) and foldhash 0.2.0 for datafusion-common 55.1.0 plus hashbrown 0.16.1 and 0.17.1.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Re-run `cargo tree -i foldhash` after petgraph, tokio-util, and hashbrown widen their ranges; delete this exception the first time a single foldhash line remains.

exceptions.reason: Three lines coexist. Examples of the normal and build introducers: getrandom 0.2.17 via ring 0.17.14 and the proc-macro const-random-macro 0.1.16 (via const-random 0.1.18 and ahash 0.8.12); getrandom 0.3.4 via ahash 0.8.12 and rand_core 0.9.5; getrandom 0.4.3 via rand 0.10.3, tempfile 3.27.0, uuid 1.26.1, and the build dependency jobserver 0.1.35 (via cc 1.4.7).
exceptions.replacement_plan: Ring is not the only holder of the 0.2 line; const-random-macro reaches it through ahash. Re-check the version-qualified inverse getrandom trees after the ring/rustls, rand, and const-random release trains; delete the exception only when a single getrandom line remains.

exceptions.reason: Four lines coexist: hashbrown 0.14.5 via dashmap 6.2.1, hashbrown 0.15.5 via petgraph 0.8.3 and tokio-util 0.7.19, hashbrown 0.16.1 via kube-runtime 4.2.0, and hashbrown 0.17.1 via arrow-array and parquet 59.3.0, DataFusion 55.1.0, indexmap 2.14.2, and lru 0.18.4.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Each line tracks a distinct upstream family. Re-run `cargo tree -i hashbrown` quarterly and collapse as kube-runtime, petgraph, tokio-util, and dashmap widen their ranges; keep the entry only while more than one line remains.

exceptions.reason: Build-time-only duplicate: heck 0.4.1 via ouroboros_macro 0.18.5; heck 0.5.0 via clap_derive 4.6.7 and the prost-build 0.14.4 build dependency. None of these are linked into a Velorix binary.
exceptions.replacement_plan: ouroboros_macro is the last heck 0.4 consumer. Re-check the version-qualified inverse heck trees and retire the exception when ouroboros_macro is replaced, upgraded to heck 0.5, or dropped from the graph.

exceptions.reason: Velorix authority paths and slatedb 0.16.0 select object_store 0.14.2, while DataFusion's object_store 0.13 (0.13.2) comes via datafusion 55.1.0 and parquet 59.3.0. The scan boundary receives SQL text, so no object_store type crosses it.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Unify authority and scan object_store clients when DataFusion widens its object_store requirement to 0.14; then delete this exception and keep only the authority-path pin. Until then keep 0.14 on authority create/read/list/range behavior without weakening create-only semantics.

exceptions.reason: rand 0.9.5 comes from DataFusion 55.1.0 crates, fail-parallel 0.6.0, slatedb 0.16.0, slatedb-common 0.16.0, and ulid 1.2.1; rand 0.10.3 comes from object_store 0.14.2.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Both lines are pinned by release trains. Re-check the version-qualified inverse rand trees after the SlateDB and object_store upgrades and delete the exception when the DataFusion and SlateDB families reach 0.10.

exceptions.reason: rand_core 0.9.5 comes from rand 0.9.5, rand_chacha 0.9.0, and rand_xoshiro 0.7.0; rand_core 0.10.1 comes from chacha20 0.10.2, getrandom 0.4.3, and rand 0.10.3.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Converges with the rand exception. Re-check the version-qualified inverse rand_core trees alongside the rand trees and delete this entry when a single rand_core line remains.

exceptions.reason: thiserror 1.0.69 comes only from slatedb 0.16.0 and slatedb-txn-obj 0.16.0; thiserror 2.0.20 is used by kube-client, kube-core, and kube-runtime 4.2.0, object_store 0.13.2 and 0.14.2, duration-str 0.11.3, json-patch 4.2.0, jsonpath-rust 1.0.11, and the Velorix workspace crates.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Track the next SlateDB 0.16.x patch that moves to thiserror 2. Re-run `cargo tree -i thiserror` after each SlateDB update and delete the entry once slatedb and slatedb-txn-obj select 2.0.20.

exceptions.reason: thiserror-impl 1.0.69 and 2.0.20 follow the thiserror 1.0.69 (slatedb) and 2.0.20 (kube, object_store, Velorix crates) split. Both are build-time proc macros and are not linked into Velorix binaries.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Remove together with the thiserror exception once SlateDB advances. Re-check with `cargo tree -i thiserror-impl` in the same pass as `cargo tree -i thiserror`.

exceptions.reason: winnow 0.6.26 comes from duration-str 0.11.3; winnow 0.7.15 comes from toml_edit 0.22.27 via toml 0.8.23.
exceptions.replacement_plan: duration-str is the only 0.6 consumer. Re-run `cargo tree -i winnow` after a duration-str release and delete the entry when duration-str selects 0.7.15.

exceptions.reason: base64 0.23.1 is used by arrow-cast 59.3.0, datafusion-functions 55.1.0, object_store 0.14.2, parquet 59.3.0, reqwest 0.13.5, and velorix-meta; base64 0.22.1 is used by hyper-util 0.1.20, k8s-openapi 0.28.0, kube-client 4.2.0, pem 3.0.6, rhizadb 0.19.0, serde-saphyr 0.0.29, tonic 0.14.6, and tower-http 0.6.11. The pem 4.0.0 -> base64 0.23.1 edge is dev-only and is excluded here.
exceptions.replacement_plan: The 0.22.1 line is held by the HTTP, Kubernetes, and Rhiza metadata stacks. Re-check the version-qualified inverse base64 trees after kube, tonic, and rhizadb upgrades and delete the entry when those families select 0.23.1; retain standard padded wire-format compatibility tests either way.

exceptions.reason: crypto-common 0.1.7 is required by digest 0.10.7, which comes from crc-fast 1.10.0 via object_store 0.14.2; crypto-common 0.2.2 is required by digest 0.11.3, which comes from md-5 0.11.0 and sha2 0.11.0.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Retire together with the digest exception once object_store 0.14.x moves crc-fast to a digest 0.11 line. Verify with `cargo tree -i crypto-common` in the same pass as `cargo tree -i digest`.

exceptions.reason: digest 0.10.7 comes from crc-fast 1.10.0 (object_store 0.14.2); digest 0.11.3 comes from md-5 0.11.0 and sha2 0.11.0.
exceptions.replacement_plan: crc-fast is the single 0.10 consumer. Re-check `cargo tree -i digest` after each object_store upgrade and drop the exception once crc-fast selects 0.11.3.

exceptions.reason: itertools 0.14.0 is used by object_store 0.13.2, prost-derive 0.14.4, and the prost-build 0.14.4 build dependency; itertools 0.15.0 is used by DataFusion 55.1.0 crates and object_store 0.14.2.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Converges with the object_store exception: once DataFusion moves off object_store 0.13.2 the 0.14 line is limited to the prost build/derive family. Re-check the version-qualified inverse itertools trees after each DataFusion release train.

exceptions.reason: Build-time-only duplicate. Examples of syn 2.0.119 introducers are kube-derive 4.2.0, prost-derive 0.14.4, sqlparser_derive 0.5.0, thiserror-impl 1.0.69, and several proc-macro support crates. Examples of syn 3.0.6 introducers are serde_derive 1.0.229, clap_derive 4.6.7, datafusion-macros 55.1.0, thiserror-impl 2.0.20, tokio-macros 2.7.2, and yoke-derive 0.8.4.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Track releases of kube-derive, prost-derive, sqlparser_derive, and thiserror 1.0.69 that adopt syn 3. Re-check the version-qualified inverse syn trees quarterly and delete the entry when only the syn 3 line remains; re-verify after any yoke-derive bump.

exceptions.reason: arrow-buffer 59.3.0 and parquet 59.3.0 use num-bigint 0.5.1, while datafusion-sql 55.1.0 still pulls bigdecimal 0.4.10 on num-bigint 0.4.8.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Follow bigdecimal's num-bigint requirement. Re-check `cargo tree -i num-bigint` after the DataFusion release train and keep query and Parquet tests intact when bigdecimal widens to 0.5.

exceptions.reason: sqlparser 0.63.0 is used by velorix-core admission; sqlparser 0.62.0 is used by datafusion, datafusion-common, datafusion-expr, and datafusion-sql 55.1.0. Admission AST types stay inside velorix-core and the DataFusion boundary receives SQL text.
exceptions.replacement_plan: Converge when DataFusion widens its parser range to 0.63. Re-check `cargo tree -i sqlparser` after each DataFusion release and retain fail-closed admission plus DataFusion query conformance tests regardless of the parser split.
